1	# Scenarios — the to-do list: add tasks and mark them done
2	
3	*Seeds. The implementation stage turns them into `.feature` files and binds the steps.*
4	
5	The register is the one `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` uses: somebody does a thing, the
6	thing "should be saved" or "should be refused as …", and the list "should hold N tasks". A task
7	is one line of text on the one shared to-do list, and it is **done** or **not done** (the words
8	of `requirements.md` § Goal). Every scenario starts from an empty to-do list, because the world is
9	cleaned before each one. `guestbook.feature` is not touched by this change, and its 22 scenarios
10	stay as they are (`SC-5`).
11	
12	**Where each seed can be seen.** The black box (`e2e/suite/`) talks to the application, not to the
13	screen. So each seed says what observes it:
14	
15	- **application**: what the application stores and gives back. The black box can bind it.
16	- **application, overlapping**: two changes must be sent before either is answered. A binding
17	  that sends them one after the other proves nothing (`requirements.md` § Self-check 19).
18	- **store-ordered**: the test has to decide which of two overlapping changes the store applies
19	  later. Only a test holding the database can do that. The black box cannot.
20	- **screen**: what the screen shows. The black box cannot see it, so its citation owner is a
21	  screen test, and choosing that owner is `design-testing`'s call. The UI smoke sees it too, but
22	  it owns no citation (`spec/design/testing.md` § The UI smoke is not a traceability surface).
23	- **person**: a person at acceptance. `R-11` is `**Verified-by:** manual`.
24	
25	**Seeds that rest on decisions `requirements.md` does not carry yet.** The user answered `Q-10`,
26	`Q-11` and `Q-12` after `requirements.md` was written, and that file still lists them as the open
27	questions `D1`, `D2` and `D3`. Five seeds depend on those answers: S-8, S-9, the last row of S-33,
28	S-49 (the "done" line), S-52 and S-53. Each one carries a comment saying which answer it rests on.
29	§ Requirements no scenario can fully observe, finding 8, reports the gap.
30	
31	## Coverage
32	| Requirement | Scenarios | Unhappy path? | Observed through |
33	|---|---|---|---|
34	| R-1 | S-1, S-2, S-3, S-4 | yes (S-4) | application; S-3 on the screen |
35	| R-2 | S-5, S-6, S-7, S-8, S-9, S-10, S-11 | yes (S-6, S-8, S-11) | application; S-10 and S-11 on the screen |
36	| R-3 | S-12, S-13, S-14, S-15, S-16, S-17, S-18, S-19, S-20 | yes (S-20); the rest are ordering, proved by comparing reads | application; S-18 store-ordered; S-19 and S-20 on the screen |
37	| R-4 | S-21, S-22, S-23, S-24, S-25 | yes (S-23, S-24) | application; S-25 on the screen, contrast half unobservable (finding 1) |
38	| R-5 | S-26, S-27, S-28, S-29, S-30 | yes (S-30, the unknown address) | screen |
39	| R-6 | S-31, S-32, S-33 | yes (S-33) | application |
40	| R-7 | S-34, S-35, S-36 | yes (S-36) | application; S-35 and S-36 on the screen |
41	| R-8 | S-37, S-38, S-39 | yes (all three) | application |
42	| R-9 | S-40, S-41, S-42, S-43 | yes (all four are conflicts) | S-40 and S-42 application, overlapping; S-41 and S-43 store-ordered |
43	| R-10 | S-44, S-45, S-46, S-47, S-48 | yes (all five) | screen |
44	| R-11 | S-49, S-50, S-51, S-52, S-53 | yes (S-50, S-51) | person (manual) |
45	
46	`R-1` clause 2 (no account, no sign-in) has no seed of its own. Every scenario here runs with
47	nobody signed in, so every one of them proves it, and no single scenario could prove it better.
48	
49	## Scenarios
50	
51	### S-1 — Adding the first task
52	```gherkin
53	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-1
54	  Scenario: Adding the first task
55	    Given the to-do list is empty
56	    When somebody adds the task "Water the plants"
57	    Then the task should be saved
58	    And the to-do list should hold 1 task
59	    And the task "Water the plants" should be shown as not done
60	```
61	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** "Water the plants" (`R-1.1`).
62	**Fails if:** nothing is stored, the task is stored as done, or its text comes back changed.
63	
64	### S-2 — The same text twice makes two separate tasks
65	```gherkin
66	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-1
67	  Scenario: The same text added twice makes two separate tasks
68	    Given the to-do list holds the task "Buy bread"
69	    When somebody adds the task "Buy bread" again
70	    And somebody marks the newer "Buy bread" as done
71	    Then the to-do list should hold 2 tasks reading "Buy bread"
72	    And the older "Buy bread" should still be shown as not done
73	```
74	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** "Buy bread" (`R-1.2`).
75	**Fails if:** a repeated text is refused or merged into the first task, or the two share one
76	identity, so that marking one marks both.
77	
78	### S-3 — A task added on the screen appears at the top without a reload
79	```gherkin
80	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-1
81	  Scenario: A task added on the screen appears at the top without reloading
82	    Given the to-do screen is open, showing the tasks "First" and "Second"
83	    When somebody adds the task "Third" on that screen
84	    Then "Third" should appear at the top of the list without the page being reloaded
85	```
86	**Observed through:** screen. **Data:** "First", "Second", "Third" (`R-1.3`).
87	**Fails if:** the screen shows a new task only after a reload, or puts it anywhere but first.
88	
89	### S-4 — A new task is never born done
90	```gherkin
91	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-1
92	  Scenario: A task sent as already done is still saved as not done
93	    Given the to-do list is empty
94	    When somebody adds the task "Already finished", sent as if it were already done
95	    Then the task should be saved
96	    And the task "Already finished" should be shown as not done
97	```
98	**Observed through:** application. Only a caller that goes around the screen can send this,
99	because the field cannot. **Data:** "Already finished" (`R-1.4`).
100	**Fails if:** the application honours a done state claimed when the task is added.
101	
102	### S-5 — A task at the boundary is accepted
103	```gherkin
104	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-2
105	  Scenario Outline: A task at the boundary size is accepted
106	    Given the to-do list is empty
107	    When somebody adds a task in which <case>
108	    Then the task should be saved
109	    And the stored text should be <kept>
110	
111	    Examples:
112	      | case | kept |
113	      | the text is at the maximum permitted length | exactly what was sent |
114	      | the text is emoji and at the maximum permitted length | exactly what was sent |
115	      | the text is decomposed accented letters and at the maximum length once composed | what was sent, with each letter composed |
116	      | the text is padded with spaces and at the maximum length after trimming | what was sent, without the spaces around it |
117	      | the text is one character long | exactly what was sent |
118	```
119	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** `tasks-boundary.json`, every case looked up by its
120	sentence (§ New fixtures; `R-2.2`, `R-2.3`, `R-2.4`, `R-2.5`).
121	**Fails if:** the application counts UTF-16 units or bytes rather than code points, measures before
122	normalizing or trimming, or places the bound anywhere but 200.
123	
124	### S-6 — A task breaking a rule is not saved
125	```gherkin
126	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-2
127	  Scenario Outline: A task breaking a rule is not saved
128	    Given the to-do list is empty
129	    When somebody tries to add a task in which <case>
130	    Then the task should be refused as <reason>
131	    And the to-do list should hold 0 tasks
132	
133	    Examples:
134	      | case | reason |
135	      | the text was not given at all | having no text |
136	      | the text is three spaces | having no text |
137	      | the text is all whitespace | having no text |
138	      | the text is two hundred and five spaces | having no text |
139	      | the text is one character too long | being too long |
140	      | the text is emoji and one code point too long | being too long |
141	      | the text is decomposed accented letters and one past the maximum once composed | being too long |
142	      | the text is padded with spaces and one character too long after trimming | being too long |
143	```
144	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** `tasks-refused.json`, every case looked up by its
145	sentence (`R-2.1`, `R-2.2`, `R-2.3`, `R-2.5`).
146	**Fails if:** an empty text is stored, the bound lets through 201, or 205 spaces are refused as
147	"too long" rather than "no text". That last one is the trim-order defect `spec/design/api.md`
148	records.
149	
150	### S-7 — Spaces between the words are kept exactly
151	```gherkin
152	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-2
153	  Scenario: Spaces between the words of a task are kept as typed
154	    Given the to-do list is empty
155	    When somebody adds the task "Buy  two   lamps"
156	    Then the task should be saved
157	    And the stored text should be exactly "Buy  two   lamps", with its two and three spaces
158	```
159	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** "Buy  two   lamps", with two spaces after "Buy" and
160	three after "two" (`R-2.6`).
161	**Fails if:** inner whitespace is squeezed or trimmed along with the edges.
162	
163	### S-8 — A task with a line break inside it is refused
164	```gherkin
165	  # Rests on Q-11 (refuse it, with its own message); R-2 clause 4 still calls it open (D2).
166	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-2
167	  Scenario: A task whose text runs over two lines is not saved
168	    Given the to-do list is empty
169	    When somebody tries to add a task in which the text has a line break between two words
170	    Then the task should be refused as being more than one line
171	    And the to-do list should hold 0 tasks
172	```
173	**Observed through:** application. Only a caller that goes around the screen can send it
174	(`Q-11`). **Data:** `tasks-refused.json` case "the text has a line break between two words",
175	whose text is "Buy bread", a line feed, then "and milk".
176	**Fails if:** the text is stored as given, stored with the break replaced, or refused with the
177	"no text" or "too long" reason instead of a reason of its own.
178	
179	### S-9 — A line break at the end of a task is trimmed like a space
180	```gherkin
181	  # Rests on Q-11's word "inside": the line break rule reads the text after trimming.
182	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-2
183	  Scenario: A line break after the last word is trimmed, not refused
184	    Given the to-do list is empty
185	    When somebody adds the task "Buy bread" with a line break after it
186	    Then the task should be saved
187	    And the stored text should be exactly "Buy bread"
188	```
189	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** "Buy bread" followed by one line feed. The line
190	feed is in the written trim set (`R-2` clause 1; `text-measurement.json` case
191	`only_the_line_feed`).
192	**Fails if:** the line break rule runs before trimming and refuses a text whose only line break
193	sits at its edge. That is the same class of defect as the one `api.md` records for measuring
194	before trimming.
195	
196	### S-10 — The field takes 200 emoji whole
197	```gherkin
198	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-2
199	  Scenario: The new-task field takes a text of 200 emoji without cutting it short
200	    Given the to-do screen is open
201	    When somebody pastes 200 grinning-face emoji into the new-task field
202	    Then the field should hold all 200 of them
203	    And the screen should let the task be added
204	```
205	**Observed through:** screen. **Data:** 200 × U+1F600, which is 400 UTF-16 code units
206	(`R-2.3`).
207	**Fails if:** the field carries a bound counted in UTF-16 units, and so stops at 100 emoji, or the
208	screen's rule refuses what the application stores. That is the `D-04` defect again.
209	
210	### S-11 — The screen refuses 201 emoji for the same reason the application does
211	```gherkin
212	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-2
213	  Scenario: The screen refuses a text of 201 emoji for the reason the application gives
214	    Given the to-do screen is open
215	    When somebody pastes 201 grinning-face emoji into the new-task field
216	    Then the field should hold all 201 of them
217	    And the screen should say the text is too long
218	    And nothing should be added to the list
219	```
220	**Observed through:** screen. **Data:** 201 × U+1F600 (`R-2.3`, `R-2` clause 5).
221	**Fails if:** the field silently cuts the text at 200 instead of saying why, or the screen's
222	reason differs from S-6's "being too long" for the same text.
223	
224	### S-12 — The newest task is at the top
225	```gherkin
226	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-3
227	  Scenario: The list shows the newest task at the top
228	    Given the to-do list holds the tasks "First", "Second" and "Third", added in that order
229	    When the to-do list is displayed
230	    Then it should read "Third", "Second", "First"
231	```
232	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** "First", "Second", "Third" (`R-3.1`).
233	**Fails if:** the list comes back oldest first, in text order, or in the order the store happens
234	to return.
235	
236	### S-13 — The list shows everything people added, done and not done alike
237	```gherkin
238	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-3
239	  Scenario: The list shows every task people added, done and not done alike
240	    Given people have already put their tasks on the list
241	    When the to-do list is displayed
242	    Then it should show every task that was added, done and not done alike
243	    And they should be ordered newest first
244	```
245	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** `tasks-ordinary.json`, in adding order. The
246	expectation is the reverse of the file, not a hand-written list.
247	**Fails if:** done tasks are filtered out or moved, a repeated text is dropped, characters
248	outside ASCII do not survive the trip, or the order is anything but newest first.
249	
250	### S-14 — A hundred and one tasks are all on one list
251	```gherkin
252	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-3
253	  Scenario: A hundred and one tasks are all shown on one list
254	    Given 101 tasks have been added, "Task 001" first and "Task 101" last
255	    When the to-do list is displayed
256	    Then all 101 tasks should be shown at once
257	    And "Task 101" should be at the top and "Task 001" at the bottom
258	```
259	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** the producing rule in § Inline values (`R-3.3`).
260	**Fails if:** the list is handed out in pieces of 20 or 100, as the guestbook's is, so that the
261	oldest task silently goes missing.
262	
263	### S-15 — Ticking a task done does not move it
264	```gherkin
265	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-3
266	  Scenario: Marking a task done leaves it where it was
267	    Given the to-do list holds the tasks "First", "Second" and "Third", added in that order
268	    When somebody marks "Second" as done
269	    Then the list should still read "Third", "Second", "First"
270	```
271	**Observed through:** application. **Data:** "First", "Second", "Third" (`R-3.4`).
272	**Fails if:** done tasks sink to the bottom or into a section of their own, or marking re-stamps
273	the moment of adding.
274	
275	### S-16 — Correcting a task does not move it to the top
276	```gherkin
277	  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-3
278	  Scenario: Correcting a task's text leaves it where it was

# Scenarios — the to-do list: add tasks and mark them done

*Seeds. The implementation stage turns them into `.feature` files and binds the steps.*

The register is the one `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` uses: somebody does a thing, the
thing "should be saved" or "should be refused as …", and the list "should hold N tasks". A task
is one line of text on the one shared to-do list, and it is **done** or **not done** (the words
of `requirements.md` § Goal). Every scenario starts from an empty to-do list, because the world is
cleaned before each one. `guestbook.feature` is not touched by this change, and its 22 scenarios
stay as they are (`SC-5`).

**Where each seed can be seen.** The black box (`e2e/suite/`) talks to the application, not to the
screen. So each seed says what observes it:

- **application**: what the application stores and gives back. The black box can bind it.
- **application, overlapping**: two changes must be sent before either is answered. A binding
  that sends them one after the other proves nothing (`requirements.md` § Self-check 19).
- **store-ordered**: the test has to decide which of two overlapping changes the store applies
  later. Only a test holding the database can do that. The black box cannot.
- **screen**: what the screen shows. The black box cannot see it, so its citation owner is a
  screen test, and choosing that owner is `design-testing`'s call. The UI smoke sees it too, but
  it owns no citation (`spec/design/testing.md` § The UI smoke is not a traceability surface).
- **person**: a person at acceptance. `R-11` is `**Verified-by:** manual`.

**Seeds that rest on decisions `requirements.md` does not carry yet.** The user answered `Q-10`,
`Q-11` and `Q-12` after `requirements.md` was written, and that file still lists them as the open
questions `D1`, `D2` and `D3`. Five seeds depend on those answers: S-8, S-9, the last row of S-33,
S-49 (the "done" line), S-52 and S-53. Each one carries a comment saying which answer it rests on.
§ Requirements no scenario can fully observe, finding 8, reports the gap.

## Coverage
| Requirement | Scenarios | Unhappy path? | Observed through |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-1 | S-1, S-2, S-3, S-4 | yes (S-4) | application; S-3 on the screen |
| R-2 | S-5, S-6, S-7, S-8, S-9, S-10, S-11 | yes (S-6, S-8, S-11) | application; S-10 and S-11 on the screen |

`R-1` clause 2 (no account, no sign-in) has no seed of its own. Every scenario here runs with
nobody signed in, so every one of them proves it, and no single scenario could prove it better.

## Scenarios

### S-1 — Adding the first task
```gherkin
  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-1
  Scenario: Adding the first task
    Given the to-do list is empty
    When somebody adds the task "Water the plants"
    Then the task should be saved
    And the to-do list should hold 1 task
    And the task "Water the plants" should be shown as not done
```
**Observed through:** application. **Data:** "Water the plants" (`R-1.1`).
**Fails if:** nothing is stored, the task is stored as done, or its text comes back changed.

### S-2 — The same text twice makes two separate tasks

```gherkin
    And the older "Buy bread" should still be shown as not done
```
**Observed through:** application. **Data:** "Buy bread" (`R-1.2`).
**Fails if:** a repeated text is refused or merged into the first task, or the two share one
identity, so that marking one marks both.

**Observed through:** application. Only a caller that goes around the screen can send this,
because the field cannot. **Data:** "Already finished" (`R-1.4`).

### S-5 — A task at the boundary is accepted
```gherkin
  @req:CR-2609-823a/R-2
  Scenario Outline: A task at the boundary size is accepted
    Given the to-do list is empty
    When somebody adds a task in which <case>
    Then the task should be saved
    And the stored text should be <kept>

    Examples:
      | case | kept |
      | the text is at the maximum permitted length | exactly what was sent |
      | the text is emoji and at the maximum permitted length | exactly what was sent |
      | the text is decomposed accented letters and at the maximum length once composed | what was sent, with each letter composed |
      | the text is padded with spaces and at the maximum length after trimming | what was sent, without the spaces around it |
      | the text is one character long | exactly what was sent |
```
**Observed through:** application. **Data:** `tasks-boundary.json`, every case looked up by its
sentence (§ New fixtures; `R-2.2`, `R-2.3`, `R-2.4`, `R-2.5`).
**Fails if:** the application counts UTF-16 units or bytes rather than code points, measures before
normalizing or trimming, or places the bound anywhere but 200.

### S-6 — A task breaking a rule is not saved
```gherkin

  Scenario Outline: A task breaking a rule is not saved
    Given the to-do list is empty
    When somebody tries to add a task in which <case>
    Then the task should be refused as <reason>
    And the to-do list should hold 0 tasks

    Examples:
      | case | reason |
      | the text was not given at all | having no text |
      | the text is three spaces | having no text |
      | the text is all whitespace | having no text |
      | the text is two hundred and five spaces | having no text |
      | the text is one character too long | being too long |
      | the text is emoji and one code point too long | being too long |
      | the text is decomposed accented letters and one past the maximum once composed | being too long |
      | the text is padded with spaces and one character too long after trimming | being too long |
```
**Observed through:** application. **Data:** `tasks-refused.json`, every case looked up by its
sentence (`R-2.1`, `R-2.2`, `R-2.3`, `R-2.5`).
**Fails if:** an empty text is stored, the bound lets through 201, or 205 spaces are refused as
"too long" rather than "no text". That last one is the trim-order defect `spec/design/api.md`
records.

### S-9 — A line break at the end of a task is trimmed like a space

## Requirements no scenario can fully observe

These are findings, not omissions. Each one names the half of a requirement that the seed above
cannot make fail.

1. **`R-4` clause 6 and the contrast half of `R-4.4`.** No suite that owns a citation can measure
   contrast. jsdom loads no application CSS. The UI smoke measures computed styles and
   `tests/fitness/test_design_tokens.py` holds every text token at 4.5:1 or better on every
   surface, but neither owns a citation (`spec/design/testing.md` § The UI smoke is not a
   traceability surface). S-25 proves "shown differently". Its contrast line has no owner unless
   `design-testing` names one, or the clause gets a manual check.
2. **`R-3.2` (two tasks with the same moment of adding).** Nobody outside the application can make
   two adds share a moment. From the black box, S-18 would pass by luck
   (`requirements.md` § Self-check 9). Only a test that stores two tasks with an equal moment can
   observe the tie-break, and that is a test with the database.
3. **`R-9` ("both before either is answered", "applied later").** The black box can send two
   changes together, which is what S-40 and S-42 need. It cannot choose which change the store
   applies later, which S-41 and S-43 need, so the deciding proof of those two belongs to a test
   that controls the interleaving. A binding that sends S-40's two changes one after the other
   passes over the whole-task write-back of race `W-1` and proves nothing
   (`requirements.md` § Self-check 19).
4. **The typing and pasting half of `R-2.3`.** Only a real browser sees a keystroke refused. A
   screen test can see that the field carries no bound counted in UTF-16 units and that the
   screen's rule agrees with the application's on the shared cases. The UI smoke sees the rest and
   owns no citation. S-10 and S-11 are written so that the first two can bind them
   (`requirements.md` § Self-check 5).
5. **`R-11` as a whole.** It is `**Verified-by:** manual`, and the black box starts the application
   with nothing filled. S-49 to S-53 are seeds for the acceptance script, not for the black box.
   `R-11.4` (every example obeys `R-2` and stays under 150 code points) has no scenario at all. The
   corpus's own fitness rules prove it (`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py`), and they own no
   citation.
6. **The "no bin, no undo, no recovery" half of `R-7` clause 2.** It is an absence. S-34 shows
   that the task does not come back after a reload. That there is no undo anywhere is a fact about
   the screen's copy and controls, and no behaviour can be made to fail on it.
7. **The confirmation itself (`R-7` clauses 1 and 3).** It exists only on the screen. In the black
   box "deletes and confirms" binds to a plain deletion. S-35 and S-36 need a screen test.
8. **`requirements.md` lags behind three answers the user has given.** `Q-11` refuses an inner line
   break "with its own message", while `R-2` clause 4 and § Open questions still hold it open as
   `D2`. `Q-10` fills each list on its own, while `R-11` clause 1 still requires "neither the
   guestbook nor the to-do list holds anything". `Q-12` puts at least one done task among the
   examples, and no clause states it. S-8, S-9, the last row of S-33, S-49's "done" line, S-52 and
   S-53 prove those answers under the tag of the requirement each would amend (`R-2`, `R-6`,
   `R-11`). The requirement text has to follow, or those seeds prove a clause nobody wrote.

## Test data

The reference corpus has two halves and they answer two different questions. **Fixtures**
(`golden-set/fixtures/`) are what a suite reads instead of inventing. **Seed data**
(`golden-set/seed/`) is what a freshly created environment opens with. A value that belongs to
both is two values. Nothing below is written into the corpus now. The implementation stage creates
it (`build-tests-integration` owns `golden-set/fixtures/` and `tests/_golden_set.py`).

### For reuse
| Fixture | What it shows | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| `golden-set/fixtures/text-measurement.json` | How a field is trimmed and how long it is, read by both languages. Its 13 single-whitespace cases (`only_the_*`, `only_every_trimmed_code_point`) and its two content cases (`zero_width_space_is_content`, `mongolian_vowel_separator_is_content`) prove the one shared rule `R-2` clause 1 borrows, so they need no copy for the task's text **as long as both sides call that one rule**. If the design gives the to-do screen a rule of its own, they are owed again for it. The task's own bound needs cases of its own, specified under § New fixtures as additions to this file. | R-2 |
| `golden-set/seed/entries-welcome.json` | The guestbook's welcome entries, unchanged. S-52 and S-53 read "the guestbook holds its welcome entries" as this file. | R-11 (via `Q-10`) |
| `golden-set/fixtures/entries-ordinary.json`, `entries-boundary.json`, `entries-refused.json` | **Not reusable, and the difference is stated.** Each holds guest book entries (a signature and a message) sized to 80 and 1000. A task is one text sized to 200. Reading a task out of them would make a task test depend on the guestbook's bounds. | none |

### New fixtures
The corpus rules apply to every file below (`golden-set/README.md`). Each file has one story,
carries a `story` and a `demonstrates` line, is named `<story>.json` in lower case with hyphens and
unique across both halves, is registered in `tests/_golden_set.py` under `FIXTURE_FILES` or
`SEED_FILES`, uses code points as its unit, and **computes its bounds from the task's own length
constant** instead of transcribing 200. Nothing in any of them looks like somebody's data: the
texts are errands with no person, place or number in them.

- **`tasks-ordinary.json`** (fixtures). The rule: the whole list, done and not done alike, is
  shown newest first, and a repeated text is two tasks. The requirements: R-3 (clauses 1 and 2),
  R-1 (clause 5). The shape: a sequence in **adding order**, six tasks, each carrying its text and
  whether it is done. Being a sequence, it has no `case` and no `description`. The loader adds all
  six in order and then marks the done ones, because a new task is never born done (`R-1.4`):

  | # (adding order) | Text | Done |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | Water the plants | no |
  | 2 | Buy bread | yes |
  | 3 | Check that café · naïve · Ærø · 日本語 · Ωμέγα survive the whole stack | no |
  | 4 | x | no |
  | 5 | Buy bread | no |
  | 6 | Call the plumber | yes |

  S-13 expects the reverse of this table. Boundary values: none; task 4 is the one-character
  minimum as an ordinary value. Personal data: none. The non-ASCII line exists to prove the round
  trip and names nobody. **No line break anywhere**, because `Q-11` refuses one, which collides
  with a corpus rule (§ Bounds the requirements did not give, item 9).
- **`tasks-boundary.json`** (fixtures). The rule: values **exactly on** the bound, every one
  accepted. The requirement: R-2. The shape: five cases, each with a `case` and a sentence a
  scenario names:

  | case | description (the sentence S-5 uses) | Text as sent | Stored as |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `text_at_maximum` | the text is at the maximum permitted length | 200 ASCII letters | the same 200 |
  | `text_at_maximum_in_emoji` | the text is emoji and at the maximum permitted length | 200 × U+1F600 (400 UTF-16 units) | the same |
  | `text_at_maximum_decomposed` | the text is decomposed accented letters and at the maximum length once composed | 200 × (U+0065 U+0301), 400 code points | 200 × U+00E9 |
  | `text_padded_to_maximum` | the text is padded with spaces and at the maximum length after trimming | 2 spaces + 200 ASCII letters + 2 spaces (204) | the 200 letters |
  | `text_at_minimum` | the text is one character long | "x" | "x" |

- **`tasks-refused.json`** (fixtures). The rule: texts the rules refuse, each naming the refusal it

  | `text_all_whitespace` | the text is all whitespace | U+0009 U+3000 U+0020 (tab, ideographic space, space; no line break, so the line-break rule cannot compete) | no text |

  | `text_padded_one_past_maximum` | the text is padded with spaces and one character too long after trimming | 2 spaces + 201 ASCII letters + 2 spaces | too long |

### Multi-day sequences
None by day. No rule here compares one day's data with an earlier day's: there is no balance and
no import. The rules that need more than one state are sequences of **two people acting on one
list**, and the order of those acts is what each scenario proves:

| Sequence | First | Then | Then | What the order proves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A screen out of date, same choice (S-23, S-24) | both see "Buy bread" in one state | somebody else marks it the other state | this person marks that same other state | a mark sets the chosen state and never flips the stored one |
| Reload (S-17) | this person reads the list: "First" | somebody else adds "From the other window" | this person reads again | the list is the application's, read fresh every time |
| Deleted underneath (S-37, S-38, S-48) | both see "Buy bread" | somebody else deletes it | this person marks it or edits it | nothing is re-created, and the refusal is the "no longer exists" one |
| Deleted twice (S-39) | "Buy bread" exists | it is deleted and confirmed | it is deleted again | a second deletion refuses rather than reports success |
| Overlapping (S-40 to S-43) | "Buy bread", not done | two changes sent, neither answered yet | both answered, list read | text and state are kept apart, and the change applied later wins within each |
| Filling (S-50, S-52, S-53) | the environment as stated | filling runs | (S-50) filling runs again | each list is filled on its own, and only while it is empty |

The corpus commits the values **on** the bound (`tasks-boundary.json`) and **one past** it
(`tasks-refused.json`). The value just below is ordinary and is listed here for completeness, not
committed.

| Rule | Just below | Exactly on the boundary | Just above |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task text length after NFC and trimming, ASCII | 199 letters, accepted | 200 letters, accepted and stored whole | 201 letters, refused as too long |
| The same, in emoji (U+1F600) | 199, accepted | 200 (400 UTF-16 units), accepted | 201, refused as too long by the screen and by the application |
| The same, decomposed (U+0065 U+0301 pairs) | 199 pairs, accepted | 200 pairs (400 code points as sent, 200 once composed), accepted and stored as 200 × U+00E9 | 201 pairs (402 as sent, 201 composed), refused as too long |
| The same, padded with two spaces each side | 2 + 199 + 2, accepted | 2 + 200 + 2 = 204 as sent, accepted and stored as the 200 | 2 + 201 + 2, refused as too long |
| Task text minimum after trimming | 0 ("", three spaces, 205 spaces), refused as no text | 1 ("x"), accepted | not a boundary |
| The UTF-16 detector | none | 101 emoji = 202 UTF-16 units, accepted (a UTF-16 counter refuses it) | none |
| Tasks in one read | 100 | 101, all shown with no pages | no ceiling is stated (reported below) |
| Contrast of a done task's text | under 4.5:1, fails | 4.5:1, passes | none |
| Example task length (seed) | none | every example stays under 150; the longest is 112 | none |

### Bounds the requirements did not give
Each item is a gap reported here, not a value chosen to fill it.

1. **Which characters count as a line break inside a task.** `Q-11` says "a line break". The seeds
   use U+000A alone, the one a caller going around the field is sure to send. Nothing says whether
   U+000D, U+000D U+000A, U+0085 (next line), U+2028, U+2029, U+000B or U+000C inside a task are
   refused too. The guestbook keeps a next line between two words of a signature
   (`text-measurement.json` case `next_line_inside_is_kept`), so the answer for a task may
   differ from the answer for a signature.
2. **Whether the line-break rule reads the text before or after trimming.** S-9 assumes after,
   from `Q-11`'s word "inside" together with `R-2` clause 1. `R-2` does not say it.
3. **Which refusal wins when one text breaks two rules.** A text over 200 code points with a line
   break inside it could be refused as "too long" or as "more than one line". No seed asserts it.
4. **A largest number of tasks.** 101 is the only size any seed uses, and it proves "no pages"
   rather than a ceiling. How many tasks the list holds or shows before one read stops being
   acceptable is unstated (`requirements.md` § Self-check 8).
5. **At least one example task not done.** `Q-12` says at least one is done. That at least one
   stays not done is what "one of the example tasks" suggests, and no floor is stated. The seed
   file shows four not done, which is inside anything the answer could mean, and S-49 does not
   assert the not-done half.
6. **A second press of "add" while the first is still unanswered** (`E-23`), **what the field holds
   after an add succeeds or fails** (`E-28`), **what the screen shows while a write waits 30 s**
   (`E-27`), and **whether the list drops a task at once after "no longer exists"**: no seed
   asserts any of them. S-37, S-38 and S-48 assert only what a reload shows and what the screen
   says.
7. **The words of every message.** "No text", "too long", "more than one line", "no longer
   exists", "not made" and "failed to load" name reasons, not copy. The copy is the mock-up's.
8. **Which change is "applied later" when two overlap.** `R-9` defines "the same moment" and leaves
   "applied later" to the store's order (`requirements.md` § Self-check 18). S-41 and S-43 name
   the later one, and only a test that controls the store's order can make that true.
9. **The corpus rules that collide with a task.** None of these is a value to pick, and each blocks
   the fixtures above until the implementation stage decides it:
   - `tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_the_corpus_exercises_a_message_with_line_breaks`
     demands a line break in every sequence file. `Q-11` refuses a line break inside a task, so
     `tasks-ordinary.json` and `tasks-welcome.json` cannot carry one, and the rule has to be
     scoped to guest book entries.
   - The corpus knows two keys, `entries` for guest book entries and `cases` for inputs to a rule
     (`golden-set/README.md` § When you add a file). A task is neither, and a task file under
     `entries` would be held to `test_every_entry_carries_the_keys_an_entry_has`.
   - `text-measurement.json` has a closed set of verdicts, and `Q-11` adds one.
10. **Who reads the task cases in the browser.** `text-measurement.json` may be read by exactly one
    frontend module, and that module sits in the guestbook's folder
    (`test_the_frontend_reads_no_corpus_file`). If the to-do screen's text rule lives in a context
    of its own, either the shared rule moves out of the guestbook's folder or the exception names
    a second reader. That choice belongs to `design-architecture` and `design-testing`.

31	### R-1: Adding a task — **P1**

33	that it joins the shared list of things to do.

35	one creates.
36	**Independent test:** Add one task to an empty list and read the list back.

39	   tasks below that field (`request.md`: "a simple view with a field for adding tasks and a list";
40	   `Q-6`: "right under the field").
41	2. The system SHALL let anybody who opens the to-do list add a task, with no account and no
42	   sign-in.
43	3. WHEN a person submits a text for a new task, the system SHALL store one task holding that
44	   text as `R-2` shapes it, record it as not done, and record its moment of adding.
45	4. WHEN a task has been added, the system SHALL show it first in the list without the person
46	   reloading the screen.
47	5. WHEN a person submits a text identical to the text of a task already on the list, the system
48	   SHALL store a second, separate task (`Q-9`).
49	
50	**Acceptance**

52	  list holds exactly one task, its text is "Water the plants", and it is shown as not done.
53	- **R-1.2** GIVEN a list holding the task "Buy bread", WHEN a person adds "Buy bread" again,
54	  THEN the list holds two tasks with that text, and marking one of them done leaves the other
55	  not done.
56	- **R-1.3** GIVEN a list of two tasks, WHEN a person adds a third, THEN the third is shown first
57	  without the page being reloaded.
58	- **R-1.4** GIVEN a request to add a task that arrives already claiming to be done, WHEN it is
59	  stored, THEN the new task is not done.
60	
61	### R-2: What is not a task is refused — **P1**
62	**Objective:** As a reader of the list, I want empty and over-long texts kept out, so that the
63	list never shows a row with nothing in it.
64	**Why this priority:** It is the other half of `R-1`. Shipping `R-1` without it stores empty
65	rows on the first day.
66	**Independent test:** Submit a text of three spaces and confirm the list is unchanged.
67	
68	1. The system SHALL normalize a task's text to Unicode NFC and trim both of its ends of the
69	   written 30-code-point whitespace set, before it measures the text. This is the rule the
70	   system already applies to every text field it accepts (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend,
71	   on `app/platform/schemas/text.py`; the set is defined in `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`).
72	2. IF a task's text is empty after trimming, THEN the system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and
73	   tell the person that a task needs text.
74	3. IF a task's text is longer than 200 code points after normalizing and trimming, THEN the
75	   system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and tell the person that the text is too long.
76	4. WHERE a text carries whitespace other than a line break between its first and last visible
77	   character, the system SHALL keep that whitespace unchanged.
78	5. The system SHALL accept on the screen exactly the texts the service accepts. The field
79	   SHALL NOT block, cut short or silently stop taking a text the service would store, and the
80	   screen SHALL NOT let through a text the service would refuse.
81	6. IF a task's text carries a line break between its first and last visible character, THEN the
82	   system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and tell the person, with a reason of its own, that a
83	   task is one line (`Q-11`: "Refuse it, with its own message"). A line break is any of U+000A,
84	   U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029: one written set that the screen and the
85	   service both read, never either language's default (assumed: `A-1`, § Named assumptions).
86	   Every one of them is in clause 1's trim set, so a line break at either end is removed by
87	   clause 1 and is not refused.

89	**Acceptance**

91	  refused, the person is told why, and the list is unchanged. The same holds for the empty text.
92	- **R-2.2** GIVEN a text of exactly 200 code points, WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted
93	  and stored whole. GIVEN one of 201 code points, THEN it is refused and the list is unchanged.
94	- **R-2.3** GIVEN a text of 200 × U+1F600 (200 code points, 400 UTF-16 code units), WHEN it is
95	  typed or pasted into the field and submitted, THEN the screen takes every character and the
96	  service stores the task. GIVEN 201 of them, THEN the screen and the service both refuse it,
97	  for the same reason.
98	- **R-2.4** GIVEN a text of 200 letters, each written as U+0065 followed by U+0301 (400 code
99	  points before normalizing, 200 after), WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted and stored as
100	  200 code points.
101	- **R-2.5** GIVEN a text of 200 code points with two spaces before it and two after (204 as

104	- **R-2.6** GIVEN the text "Buy  two   lamps", WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is stored with its

111	### R-3: One shared list, in one order — **P1**
112	**Objective:** As anybody who opens the to-do list, I want every task on one list in the order
113	the tasks were added, newest first, so that everybody reads the same list the same way.
114	**Why this priority:** The list is what a person looks at. Without a settled order two people
115	see two different lists, and a task just added gets lost among the others.
116	**Independent test:** Add three tasks, then read the list from a second browser.
117	
118	1. WHEN the to-do list is opened, the system SHALL show every stored task, done and not done
119	   alike, on one list, with no division into pages and no filter (`Q-9`).
120	2. The system SHALL order the list by moment of adding, newest first (`Q-6`).
121	3. WHERE two tasks share a moment of adding, the system SHALL show them in the same relative

123	4. WHEN a task is marked done or not done, or its text is edited, the system SHALL keep it in

147	### R-4: Marking a task done and not done — **P1**
148	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to tick a task done, and tick it back if I ticked it by
149	mistake, so that the list says what is left to do.
150	**Why this priority:** It is the point of the request: "mark that a task is done" (`request.md`).
151	**Independent test:** Tick one task done, reload, tick it back, reload.
152	
153	1. WHEN a person marks a not-done task as done, the system SHALL record it as done.
154	2. WHEN a person marks a done task as not done, the system SHALL record it as not done (`Q-2`).
155	3. WHEN a person marks a task, the system SHALL record the state the person chose, whatever
156	   state was stored at that moment: marking done a task already done leaves it done, and marking
157	   not done a task already not done leaves it not done.
158	4. WHEN a task is marked done or not done, the system SHALL leave its text unchanged.
159	5. The system SHALL show, for every task in the list, whether it is done, and SHALL show a done
160	   task differently from a not-done one (`Q-4`).
161	6. WHILE a task is shown as done, the system SHALL keep its text at or above the contrast floor

166	- **R-4.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN a person marks it done and reloads the

177	### R-5: Two screens and the way between them — **P1**
178	**Objective:** As somebody using the application, I want to move between the guestbook and the
179	to-do list, so that I can find the list without knowing its address while the guestbook stays

205	### R-6: Editing a task's text — **P2**
206	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to correct a task's text, so that a typo or a changed plan does

208	**Why this priority:** The list works without it, because delete and re-add is a workaround, but

210	**Independent test:** Edit one task's text and read it back.
211	
212	1. WHEN a person changes a task's text, the system SHALL store the new text and show it in the
213	   task's place.
214	2. WHEN a task's text is edited, the system SHALL leave the task's state as it is stored at that

219	4. IF an edited text is empty after trimming, is longer than 200 code points after normalizing

223	**Acceptance**
224	- **R-6.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bred", WHEN it is edited to "Buy bread", THEN the list
225	  shows "Buy bread", not done, in the same position.
226	- **R-6.2** GIVEN the done task "Call the plumber", WHEN it is edited to "Call the plumber again",

231	
232	### R-7: Deleting a task — **P2**
233	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to remove a task, with one question before it goes, so that a
234	list does not fill with things nobody will do and a slip of the mouse deletes nothing.
235	**Why this priority:** Useful and independent of every other operation, and in scope (`Q-3`).
236	**Independent test:** Delete one task out of three and confirm the other two remain.
237	
238	1. WHEN a person asks to delete a task, the system SHALL ask them to confirm before it deletes
239	   anything (`Q-9`).
240	2. WHEN the person confirms, the system SHALL delete the task permanently, with no bin, no undo

243	4. WHEN a task is deleted, the system SHALL leave every other task unchanged.
244	
245	**Acceptance**
246	- **R-7.1** GIVEN the tasks "Alpha", "Beta" and "Gamma", WHEN a person deletes "Beta" and
247	  confirms, THEN the list holds "Alpha" and "Gamma", and "Beta" does not come back after a reload.
248	- **R-7.2** GIVEN the task "Beta", WHEN a person asks to delete it and then cancels, THEN "Beta"
249	  is still on the list, unchanged.
250	
251	### R-8: A task that no longer exists — **P2**
252	**Objective:** As somebody whose screen is out of date, I want to be told clearly when the task I
253	am acting on has been deleted, so that I never believe I changed something that is gone.
254	**Why this priority:** Without identity anybody can delete any task, so this happens as soon as
255	two people use the list. The user asked for "a clear message" (`Q-9`).
256	**Independent test:** Delete a task through one browser, then try to mark it done through
257	another.
258	
259	1. IF a person edits, marks or deletes a task that has already been deleted, THEN the system
260	   SHALL change nothing, create no task, and tell the person the task no longer exists.
261	2. IF the same task is deleted a second time, THEN the system SHALL refuse and tell the person it

264	**Acceptance**
265	- **R-8.1** GIVEN person A's screen shows "Buy bread" and person B has deleted it, WHEN A marks it
266	  done, THEN A is told the task no longer exists, and after a reload no "Buy bread" is on the list.

268	  A is told the task no longer exists, and no task "Buy rye bread" appears.
269	- **R-8.3** GIVEN a task already deleted, WHEN it is deleted again, THEN the person is told it no
270	  longer exists.

272	### R-9: Two people changing one task at once — **P2**
273	**Objective:** As one of several people sharing the list, I want changes made at the same moment
274	to settle predictably, so that my tick is never silently undone by somebody else's edit.
275	**Why this priority:** It applies only when two people act on one task at once, but when that
276	happens and this requirement is missing, a change is lost with nothing on screen to show it.
277	**Independent test:** Send an edit and a mark for one task before either one is answered.
278	
279	1. WHEN two people change the text of the same task at the same moment, the system SHALL keep
280	   the text from the change applied later (`Q-9`: "the later change wins").
281	2. WHEN one person edits a task's text while another marks the same task at the same moment, the
282	   system SHALL keep both changes, the edited text and the chosen state, in whichever order they
283	   are applied.
284	3. WHEN two people mark the same task at the same moment, the system SHALL end with the state

286	
287	"At the same moment" means that both changes are sent before either one is answered.
288	
289	**Acceptance**
290	- **R-9.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN A edits it to "Buy rye bread" and B marks it
291	  done, both before either is answered, THEN the task reads "Buy rye bread" and is done, whichever
292	  change was applied first.
293	- **R-9.2** GIVEN the task "Buy bread", WHEN A edits it to "Buy rye bread" and B edits it to "Buy
294	  white bread", and B's change is applied later, THEN the task reads "Buy white bread".
295	- **R-9.3** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN A and B both mark it done, both before either
296	  is answered, THEN it is done.
297	
298	### R-10: A change that did not go through is not shown as made — **P2**
299	**Objective:** As somebody on a poor connection, I want to know when my change did not go
300	through, so that I never believe a task was added, ticked, edited or deleted when it was not.
301	**Why this priority:** The list belongs to the application, not to the browser (`brainstorm.md`
302	§ What was settled). A screen showing a change the application never stored lies about the one
303	thing the list is for.
304	**Independent test:** Cut the service off, tick a task, and read the screen.
305	
306	1. IF adding, marking, editing or deleting a task is not stored, because the service cannot be
307	   reached or refuses the change, THEN the system SHALL tell the person the change was not made.
308	2. IF a change was not stored, THEN the system SHALL NOT show it in the list as made.
309	3. IF the list cannot be read, THEN the system SHALL say that the list failed to load and SHALL NOT
310	   say that the list is empty.
311	
312	**Acceptance**
313	- **R-10.1** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN a person marks "Buy bread" done, THEN the
314	  screen says the change was not made and "Buy bread" is shown as not done.
315	- **R-10.2** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN a person adds a task, THEN the screen says
316	  the task was not added and no new task appears in the list.
317	- **R-10.3** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN the to-do list is opened, THEN the screen
318	  says the list failed to load, and does not show the empty-list sentence of `R-3.6`.
319	
320	### R-11: Example tasks in a new environment — **P3**
321	**Objective:** As a reviewer opening a freshly created environment, I want a few example tasks
322	already on the list, so that I can judge the screen without typing.
323	**Why this priority:** The list works without it. A preview with an empty list gives nobody
324	anything to judge (`Q-8`).
325	**Independent test:** Bring up a freshly created environment and open the to-do list.
326	**Verified-by:** manual — the seeder is proved by `tests/tooling/` and the seed corpus by `tests/fitness/`, neither of which carries a requirement citation by rule (`spec/design/testing.md` § The UI smoke is not a traceability surface), and the black box starts the application with `--no-seed`; a person opens a freshly created environment and counts the example tasks.
327	
328	1. WHEN an environment whose to-do list holds no task is filled with example data, whatever the
329	   guestbook holds, the system SHALL put at least three example tasks on the to-do list (`Q-10`:
330	   "Yes, each list is filled on its own").
331	2. The system SHALL hold every example task to the text rules of `R-2`, and SHALL keep every
332	   example task under 150 code points (the seed corpus is looked at, not a boundary file).
333	3. IF the environment is production, THEN the system SHALL add no example task
334	   (`spec/design/architecture.md` § What a new environment starts with).
335	4. IF the to-do list already holds at least one task, THEN the system SHALL add no example task,
336	   so that filling an environment again never duplicates them.
337	5. WHEN an environment is filled with example data, the system SHALL decide whether to give the
338	   guestbook its welcome entries by what the guestbook holds alone, whatever the to-do list holds
339	   (`Q-10`).
340	6. WHEN the example tasks have been put on the to-do list, the system SHALL mark at least one of
341	   them done (`Q-12`: "Yes, at least one is done"). It is added not done and then marked, because
342	   a new task is never born done (`R-1` clause 3).
343	
344	**Acceptance**
345	- **R-11.1** GIVEN a freshly created environment, WHEN it has been filled with example data, THEN
346	  the to-do list shows at least three tasks.
347	- **R-11.2** GIVEN an environment whose to-do list holds one task, WHEN it is filled with example
348	  data again, THEN the list still holds exactly that one task.
349	- **R-11.3** GIVEN a production environment, WHEN filling it with example data is attempted, THEN
350	  no task is added.
351	- **R-11.4** GIVEN the example tasks, WHEN each is measured by the rules of `R-2`, THEN each is
352	  accepted and none reaches 150 code points.
353	- **R-11.5** GIVEN an environment whose guestbook holds its welcome entries and whose to-do list is
354	  empty, WHEN it is filled, THEN the list shows the example tasks and the guestbook holds exactly
355	  the entries it held before.
356	- **R-11.6** GIVEN a to-do list holding one task and an empty guestbook, WHEN it is filled, THEN
357	  the guestbook gets its welcome entries and the list still holds exactly that one task.
358	- **R-11.7** GIVEN a to-do list just filled with example tasks, WHEN it is shown, THEN at least one
359	  example task is shown as done.

465	### Races
466	- **W-1: an edit against a mark on one task.** The read-then-write: the edit reads the stored
467	  task (text and state), replaces the text and writes the whole task back. Between that read and
468	  that write the mark has stored "done". What the database holds at that moment is "done", and
469	  the edit's write-back replaces it with the "not done" it read. `R-9` clause 2 and `R-6`
470	  clause 2 forbid that outcome. The only update path in the codebase today overwrites with no
471	  version check (`impact.md`, `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:206`), so
472	  nothing in the store holds this rule yet (constitution, article VI). Only a concurrent test can
473	  tell the two apart (`spec/design/testing.md` § Choosing what proves what).
474	- **W-2: two marks from screens that are out of date.** The read-then-write happens if a mark is
475	  built as "read the state, store its opposite". A reads not done and stores done. B, who saw not
476	  done on the screen, reads done and stores not done. The database ends "not done", although both
477	  people chose done. `R-4` clause 3 (record the chosen state) removes the read.
478	- **W-3: an edit or a mark against a delete.** The read-then-write: the edit reads the task (it
479	  exists), the delete removes it, then the edit writes. What the database holds at that moment is
480	  no task. A write that creates on absence brings the task back. `R-8` clause 1 ("create no task")
481	  forbids it.
482	- **W-4: two adds in the same instant.** There is no read. Both tasks are stored with the same
483	  moment of adding, and only a tie-break makes the order total (`R-3` clause 3).
484	- **W-5: filling a new environment against a person adding.** The read-then-write: filling reads
485	  "the to-do list is empty", a person adds a task, then filling posts the example tasks. The
486	  database ends with the person's task plus the examples. No constraint stands behind the check.
487	  The guestbook's filling has the same exposure today, and it is rare, because it only happens in
488	  the seconds after a new environment comes up.
489	- **W-6: two fillings of one environment.** Deploy and preview both run on one environment.
490	  Both read "empty" and both post, so the examples appear twice. This is rare, and the guestbook
491	  has the same exposure today.
492	
493	### With no defined behaviour
494	- When a person presses "add" a second time before the first add is answered, does the second
495	  press add a second task, or is it held off until the first is answered?
496	- After an add fails, does the field keep what was typed? After an add succeeds, is the field
497	  emptied?
498	- What does the screen show while a write waits 30 s for its answer, and can the person act on
499	  other tasks meanwhile?
500	- Is there a largest number of tasks the list holds or shows? With no pages (`Q-9`), every task
501	  is read at once, and nothing bounds how many there are.
502	- After "the task no longer exists" (`R-8`), does the list drop that task at once or on the next
503	  reload?

640	    renumbers or edits them.
641	
642	## Non-Goals
643	- **Removing or changing the guestbook.** The user chose to keep it beside the list (`Q-1`), and
644	  every guestbook behaviour and suite stays as it is (`SC-5`).
645	- **A Polish screen or any translation.** The screen is English, like the rest (`Q-7`,
646	  `spec/design/conventions.md` § Language).
647	- **Search, pages, filters (for example "only open tasks") and a "clear all done" action.**
648	  Everything is on one list (`Q-9`). `BR-05` stays the guestbook's.
649	- **Due dates, priorities, assigned people, categories and more than one list.** It is one shared
650	  list of one-line tasks (`Q-9`).
651	- **Live updates.** Other people's changes appear when the list is reloaded (`Q-9`, `R-3`
652	  clause 5). Nothing pushes them to an open screen.
653	- **Accounts, sign-in, "my tasks", and recording who added or ticked a task.** This is the
654	  standing non-goal (`spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals): anybody adds, marks, edits and
655	  deletes any task.
656	- **Moderation.** The same standing non-goal: no reports, no hiding.
657	- **Warning a person that somebody else's change overwrote theirs.** "The later change wins"
658	  (`Q-9`), and nobody is told their change was replaced (`R-9`).
659	- **A bin, undo, or restoring a deleted task.** "Gone for good" (`Q-9`, `R-7` clause 2).
660	- **Moving done tasks to the bottom or into a separate section.** Ticking never moves a task
661	  (`Q-4`, `R-3` clause 4).
662	- **Reordering tasks by hand.** The order is the moment of adding, newest first (`Q-6`), and
663	  nothing else sets it.
664	- **A mobile design of the new screen.** This is the standing non-goal (`spec/invariants.md`
665	  § Deliberate non-goals, "A mobile version").
666	- **A retention policy for tasks.** A task lives until somebody deletes it, as an entry does
667	  under the standing non-goal. For tasks this is assumed, not decided (`A-2`, § Named
668	  assumptions).
669	- **Detecting a duplicate caused by a retried add.** The same text twice is two tasks by
670	  decision (`Q-9`, `R-1` clause 5), so `E-20` leaves a duplicate for a person to delete.
671	
672	## Bounds
673	
674	| Quantity | Value | Where it comes from |
675	|---|---|---|
676	| Task text, maximum | 200 code points, after NFC normalization and trimming | `Q-9` ("up to 200 characters"). The unit is the one every text field is measured in (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend on `text.py`; `spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters) |
677	| Task text, minimum | 1 code point after trimming | `Q-9` ("An empty task, or one made only of spaces, is refused") |
678	| Trim set | the written 30-code-point set | `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`, `app/platform/schemas/text.py` |
679	| Line break inside a task | refused; the set is U+000A, U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029 | `Q-11` for the refusal; the set is assumption `A-1` (§ Named assumptions) |
680	| Emoji boundary value | 200 × U+1F600 = 200 code points = 400 UTF-16 code units; 201 refused | `R-2.3`, from the `D-04` incident |
681	| Decomposed boundary value | 200 × (U+0065 U+0301) = 400 code points before NFC, 200 after | `R-2.4`, from `BR-01`'s normalization |
682	| Padding boundary value | 2 + 200 + 2 = 204 as typed, accepted; 205 spaces, refused as empty | `R-2.5`, from the `api.md` trim-order incident |
683	| Tasks shown per read | all of them, with no pages | `Q-9` |
684	| List size that proves "no pages" | 101 tasks | one more than 100, the guestbook's largest piece (`spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters), and more than its default of 20 |
685	| Example tasks, minimum | 3 | `Q-8` ("a few"), with the seed-half rule that a list is at least three items (`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_the_seed_half_shows_a_list_rather_than_an_entry`) |
686	| Example tasks done, minimum | 1 | `Q-12` |
687	| Example task, maximum length | under 150 code points (0.75 × 200) | the seed-half margin in `tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_no_seed_entry_stands_near_a_published_limit` |
688	| Contrast of a done task's text | at least 4.5:1 against the surface behind it | `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens (WCAG 2.1, 1.4.3) |
689	| "At the same moment" | both changes sent before either is answered | `R-9` |
690	
691	The search phrase's bound is also 200 code points (`QUERY_MAX_LENGTH`). That is two rules
692	sharing a number, and a test that reads the phrase's constant to prove the task's bound proves
693	the wrong rule.
694	
695	## Open questions
696	- **`D1`: answered.** `Q-10` → A, each list is filled on its own (`R-11` clause 1).
697	- **`D2`: answered.** `Q-11` → A, refuse it with its own message (`R-2` clause 6).
698	- **`D3`: answered.** `Q-12` → A, at least one example is done (`R-11` clause 6).
699	- **Double add while the first is in flight, what the field holds after an add, the screen while
700	  a write waits, the list after "no longer exists", and a largest number of tasks.** None of
701	  these blocks the requirements. They are for the design stage: the screen specification and the
702	  mock-up the user approves. A product rule the design needs from them goes back to the user,
703	  not into a design document.
704	- **The frame's words with two screens: the lockup name, the footer about "entries", the header
705	  fact, and where the not-found page leads.** These block nothing here. `brainstorm.md` § Open
706	  gives them to the mock-up, for the user to approve there. `R-5` clause 4 is the only
707	  constraint on them in this document.
708	
709	## Named assumptions
710	
711	*This stage's question budget is spent: `sdd-engine loop ask --raise` refused a thirteenth
712	question. What no answer decides is written here as an assumption, in the form "Assumed: …, say
713	so if not". Neither item below is a human decision yet. The user confirms or overrules each one
714	at the approval of this document, which ends the stage.*
715	
716	- **`A-1`: which characters are a line break (`R-2` clause 6, `R-6` clause 4).** Assumed: a line
717	  break is any of U+000A (line feed), U+000B (line tabulation), U+000C (form feed), U+000D
718	  (carriage return), U+0085 (next line), U+2028 (line separator) and U+2029 (paragraph
719	  separator): one written set that the screen and the service both read, so a pasted text is
720	  refused the same way on both sides. Say so if not. The other reading is U+000A and U+000D
721	  alone, which keeps the other five as content inside a task, the way a guestbook signature keeps
722	  U+0085 (`text-measurement.json` case `next_line_inside_is_kept`). The set is written down
723	  because the two languages' own line-break defaults disagree, among others about U+000B, U+000C
724	  and U+0085 (COH-requirements-4 in `review/coherence.md`), and `R-2` clause 5 fails if each side
725	  takes its own. **Status:** assumed, awaiting the user.
726	- **`A-2`: a task lives until somebody deletes it (§ Non-Goals).** Assumed: nothing removes a
727	  task except a person deleting it, with no expiry and no retention policy, as for a guestbook
728	  entry (`spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals, "A data retention policy"). Say so if not.
729	  `Q-9` settled that anybody may delete any task and that a deleted task is gone for good. It did
730	  not settle whether a task can go without anybody deleting it. Until this is confirmed, that
731	  non-goal keeps its wording for entries alone. **Status:** assumed, awaiting the user.
732	
733	## Self-check
734	
735	1. [Completeness] [§ R-1] Does the moment of adding need to be visible to anybody, or does it
736	   serve only the order? If a person has to see it, the screen needs a requirement and the
737	   mock-up a place for it. As written, it serves `R-3` alone.
738	2. [Coherence] [§ R-1] Is "a new task is recorded not done, whatever the request claims" a rule
739	   the user stated, or one inferred from "a to-do list"? If a reviewer calls it invented, it goes
740	   to the user. The rejected reading is that a client can add a task already done.
741	3. [Clarity] [§ R-2] Can a second implementer find "the written 30-code-point set" without
742	   reading guestbook code? It points at `BR-01` and `text.py`. If tasks land in another context,
743	   the set has to be shared rather than copied, or two copies drift.
744	4. [Completeness] [§ R-2] What happens to a line break inside a text? It is refused with a reason
745	   of its own (`Q-11`, `R-2` clause 6, `R-2.7`). Which characters are a line break is assumption
746	   `A-1`, for the user to confirm at this document's approval.
747	5. [Measurability] [§ R-2] Can "the screen takes every character" in `R-2.3` be observed in a
748	   suite that owns citations? It can over the rule the screen applies, in vitest. The typing and
749	   pasting half only the UI smoke sees, and the smoke owns no citation. If design finds no vitest
750	   seam, that half loses its automated proof.
751	6. [Compliance] [§ R-2] Does `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` hold the new 200 and its
752	   browser copy? No, it names three bounds. Unless it is extended, the new copy stands unheld, as
753	   the signature's unit did before `D-04`.
754	7. [Clarity] [§ R-3] Does "newest first" still mean "by moment of adding" after an edit? Yes, by
755	   clause 4. A reader who takes "newest" as "most recently changed" makes edited tasks jump, and
756	   `R-3.4` pins the intended reading.
757	8. [Completeness] [§ R-3] Is there a number of tasks beyond which "every task on one list" stops
758	   being acceptable? None is stated. If the design needs a ceiling, that is a product question for
759	   the user, not a design choice.
760	9. [Measurability] [§ R-3] Can `R-3.2` be observed without control of the clock? Only if a test
761	   can store two tasks with an equal moment of adding. Otherwise the tie-break passes by luck.
762	10. [Clarity] [§ R-4] Is "mark done" setting a chosen state, or flipping the stored one? It is
763	    written as setting (clause 3). A flip built by the design fails `R-4.3` and `R-9.3` under
764	    screens that are out of date.
765	11. [Coherence] [§ R-4] Does clause 6 restate a rule that already has a home
766	    (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens)? Yes, on purpose, as the observable form of the
767	    defect this screen invites. If the frame's floor moves, this clause follows it rather than
768	    competing with it.
769	12. [Measurability] [§ R-4] Can "shown differently" be judged without a person? Only through what
770	    a test can read, such as the done state as the page exposes it. The visual form belongs to the
771	    mock-up.
772	13. [Completeness] [§ R-5] Where does the not-found page lead when there are two screens? That is
773	    not stated. If it leads only to the guestbook, a visitor who wanted the to-do list is one step
774	    further away, which `R-5` does not forbid.
775	14. [Compliance] [§ R-5] Would a navigation link named exactly "Guestbook" break the exact lookups
776	    in `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py`? Yes: two links with one name. The design either names the link
777	    differently, or the smoke's locator changes in the same change.
778	15. [Coherence] [§ R-6] Does "leave the task's state as it is stored at that moment" contradict
779	    "the later change wins"? Only if "later wins" is read as applying to the whole task. It is
780	    read per aspect (text, state). If the user meant the whole task, `R-9` clause 2 is the
781	    sentence to take back to them.
782	16. [Completeness] [§ R-7] Does the confirmation have to name the task? That is not stated. The
783	    guestbook's dialog does name the entry (`spec/design/ui/guestbook.md` § The delete dialog), so
784	    the mock-up will likely copy it. It is not a requirement here.
785	17. [Clarity] [§ R-8] Does "tell the person the task no longer exists" require the list to drop
786	    that task at once? No, and it is open. If the design leaves it on screen, a second attempt
787	    meets the same message.
788	18. [Clarity] [§ R-9] Is "the change applied later" well defined when two requests overlap? It
789	    means the one whose write the store applied last. If a reviewer needs arrival order instead, a
790	    mechanism beyond the store's own ordering is needed.
791	19. [Measurability] [§ R-9] Can `R-9.1` be proved by a sequential test? No. An edit followed by a
792	    mark passes over a whole-task write-back too. Only concurrent requests tell the two apart
793	    (constitution, article VI).
794	20. [Completeness] [§ R-10] Is the typed text still in the field after a failed add? That is open.
795	    If it is not, the person retypes it, and nothing here says whether that is acceptable.
796	21. [Completeness] [§ R-11] What happens in an environment that existed before this change and
797	    whose to-do list is empty? That is `D1`, answered by `Q-10` → A (`R-11` clause 1). Option A
